title: Judge sets June 2028 trial in the Charlie Kirk murder case; Kirk's family calls the delay disappointing
dek: After weeks of argument over the date, a Utah judge picked one between what prosecutors and the defense asked for. Erika Kirk's statement on it spread widely.
what: On Monday, 9 November 2026, Judge Tony Graf in Utah set the trial of the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk. NBC News and Fox News report jury selection begins on 21 June 2028 and the court has reserved 105 days.

The sides had asked for different dates. Fox News reports prosecutors preferred 31 January 2028 with October 2027 as a fallback, the defense proposed late 2029, and Erika Kirk asked for a trial by October 2027.

NBC News reports the judge said the schedule protects the rights of both the accused and Mrs. Kirk, and that both sides need time to review about 8 million digital items and 3.3 terabytes of evidence. Fox News reports he also cited the holidays and a defense lawyer's federal trial in January 2028. NBC reports the Kirk family accepted the June 2028 date.

Erika Kirk's account posted a family statement calling the decision to delay the trial "deeply disappointing" and saying every extra day "prolongs our family's pain". The man is accused of aggravated murder and other counts. He is presumed innocent until a verdict. This page does not name him.
why: The date is the first fixed point in a case that has been waiting on one for weeks, and the family's statement put the cost of the delay in plain words.
next: The date can still move if either side asks the court to change it.
